table_title: List the 17 Formula One drivers with 2 or more World Drivers' Championships, per Wikipedia's `List of Formula One World Drivers' Champions` master article's 'By driver' summary table. Aggregation = COUNT(championships) GROUP BY driver, filtered to count ≥ 2; with MIN(year) as First Title Year and MAX(year) as Last Title Year. Universe spans 76 F1 seasons 1950-2025 (35 unique champions total; 17 with ≥2 titles, 18 with exactly 1 title — including Lando Norris 2025 first-time champion). Sort = Championship Count DESC primary, First Title Year ASC secondary tiebreak (chronological-first within count tier).
db_analog: SELECT c.driver, COUNT(*) AS championship_count, MIN(c.season_year) AS first_title_year, MAX(c.season_year) AS last_title_year FROM f1_world_drivers_championships c WHERE c.season_year BETWEEN 1950 AND 2025 GROUP BY c.driver HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, MIN(c.season_year) ASC
temporal_note: Wikipedia 'List of Formula One World Drivers' Champions' master article accessed 2026-05-20. Universe = 17 drivers with ≥2 World Drivers' Championships from the master article's 'By driver' summary table. The master article covers 76 F1 seasons (1950 Farina through 2025 Norris) with 35 unique champions; the ≥2-titles filter yields 17 drivers (current as of post-2025-season). temporal_sensitivity = medium because the ≥2-titles universe shifts when a single-time champion wins a second title (most recent transition: Verstappen 2021→2022 moved him from single-time to multi-time; before that, Vettel 2010→2011; Hamilton 2008→2014). Lando Norris winning the 2025 championship as his first title does NOT alter the ≥2-titles universe (Norris remains in the 18-driver single-time-champion bucket). Future transitions possible: Norris could join the universe in 2026+ if he wins a second title; other current single-time champions (Räikkönen, Button, N. Rosberg, Villeneuve) are retired so cannot transition. Source priority: all 4 cells per row come from the master article — Driver name from 'By driver' table's Driver column verbatim; Championship Count from 'By driver' table's Titles column; First Title Year + Last Title Year derived from MIN/MAX of the master's Years-Won column entries per row (the master lists each driver's championship years in a single cell; MIN/MAX is benchmark-curator aggregation over master-supplied list values). Driver names preserve master verbatim including accented characters (Mika Häkkinen with umlaut).
_extraction_notes: Aggregation instance — COUNT(championships) GROUP BY driver HAVING COUNT≥2 over master article's 76-row season-champion list. PIVOT context: 6th of 13 floor-lift instances toward 102-target after multiple set_filter source-friction attempts (canals duplicate; lighthouses fragmented; IGOs fragmented; UNESCO Danger List 403; glaciers fragmented; volcanic-eruptions VEI≥5 set-filter-vs-comparative ambiguity); 5 prior floor lifts: epidemics-1M lifting comparative + WWI battles lifting multi_hop + industrial-disasters lifting causal + world-expositions lifting temporal + antarctic-stations lifting set_filter. F1 championships has the cleanest aggregation shape: master article literally has a 'By driver' summary table providing pre-aggregated counts + year lists, supporting source-defined aggregation without curator computation beyond MIN/MAX over master-supplied year lists. Brings `aggregation` from 5/5 (floor met, just-saturated by existing 5 instances including `scotus_appointment_rows_by_president_mckinley_through_biden` + `clubs_with_at_least_2_european_cup_and_uefa_champions_league_titles`) to **6/5** = 6th of 13 floor-lift instances toward 102-target. Sports/Motorsport NEW subdomain under Sports family per domain_taxonomy.md preferred Family/Subdomain pattern (Sports used for Football, Olympics, Records precedents; Motorsport genuinely novel). people/race-car-drivers NEW fine-class within people bucket extending people fine-classes (joining astronauts, authors, judges, philosophers, physicists, mountaineers, monarchs, diplomats, presidents, justices, etc.). Schema: 4 cols (Driver PK + Championship Count numeric + First Title Year numeric + Last Title Year numeric). Sort: Championship Count DESC primary, First Title Year ASC secondary tiebreak — chronological-first within count tier (e.g., 7-titles tier: Schumacher 1994 first then Hamilton 2008; 4-titles tier: Prost 1985 first then Vettel 2010 then Verstappen 2021; 3-titles tier: Brabham 1959 first; 2-titles tier: Ascari 1952 first). Per-row source: all 4 cells per row from master's 'By driver' summary table — Driver + Championship Count come verbatim from the master; First Title Year + Last Title Year computed as MIN/MAX over the master's Years-Won column list (curator aggregation, NOT separate source). source_count = 1 with manual_wikipedia gt_construction. claim_type = source_defined because the 17-driver universe is precisely what the master's 'By driver' table enumerates when filtered to Titles ≥ 2 (no curator selection beyond the threshold filter; threshold ≥2 is a benchmark-defined cutoff that separates multi-champion drivers from single-time champions). Universe count = 17 (per master's table); domain-specific stats: Championship Count range 2-7 (max Schumacher=Hamilton tied at 7); First Title Year range 1951 (Fangio) to 2021 (Verstappen); Last Title Year range 1953 (Ascari) to 2024 (Verstappen); national distribution UK 4 (Hamilton, Stewart, G. Hill, Clark), Brazil 3 (Senna, Piquet, Fittipaldi), Germany 2 (Schumacher, Vettel), Argentina 1 (Fangio), France 1 (Prost), Netherlands 1 (Verstappen), Australia 1 (Brabham), Austria 1 (Lauda), Italy 1 (Ascari), Finland 1 (Häkkinen), Spain 1 (Alonso). Aggregation justification: master's 'By driver' summary table directly provides pre-aggregated count + year-list per driver; threshold filter ≥2 separates the 17 multi-champion drivers from the 18 single-time champions (Norris 2025 most recent single-time). HAVING-clause semantics: SELECT driver, COUNT(*), MIN(year), MAX(year) FROM season-champion-list GROUP BY driver HAVING COUNT >= 2 — pure aggregation pattern with grouping + count + min/max + having-filter.
